title: API: a fully failed deactivate returns updated [] with no history, and a repeated id counts once
custom_preconds: Env https://sv10647.qa.shopview.com, S2 shop. Location Staging Heavy Duty. Logged in as (a) Admin or a default Parts Manager. API replay from Chrome DevTools against sv10647api.qa.shopview.com with header X-Location-ID = the current location (Copy as fetch from a request of the logged-in session, then edit method, path and body). QAPL-I2 and QAPL-I3 are inactive; all 201 QAPL-CAP parts are active. Collect the ids of 200 QAPL-CAP parts by paging through GET /api/inventory/parts?status=active&search=QAPL-CAP.
custom_steps:
1. PATCH /api/inventory/parts/status with body {"partIds":["<QAPL-I2 id>","<QAPL-I3 id>"],"status":"inactive","note":"QA all fail"}.
  2. Open QAPL-I2's and QAPL-I3's Part History.
  3. PATCH /api/inventory/parts/status with the 200 distinct QAPL-CAP ids plus one of them repeated (201 entries), "status":"inactive" and "note":"QA repeat".
  4. Open the Part History of the repeated part.
  5. PATCH /api/inventory/parts/status with the same 200 distinct ids and "status":"active" (restore).
custom_expected:
1. 200; data.updated is []; data.failed lists both with "Part is already in that state."
  2. No "Deactivated | Reason: QA all fail" entry was written on either part (no DB access: this stands in for the DB check of no entity_event rows).
  3. 200 (not 400 "Select 200 parts or fewer."); data.updated lists the 200 parts, the repeated id only once; data.failed is [].
  4. Exactly one "Deactivated | Reason: QA repeat" entry.
  5. 200; data.updated lists the 200 parts; they are back on the Active tab.
